content_of_post_to_answer: Why do some people who experience similar childhoods end up with different levels of honesty and transparency?
answer: Similar childhoods don't necessarily teach the same lesson. One child learns that honesty creates connection; another learns that telling the truth invites punishment, rejection, or humiliation. Both may be adapting intelligently to the same kind of environment. I've explored this pattern further on my profile, because it raises a deeper question: when does a childhood survival strategy become an adult's definition of character?
